newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Andrew gas flowing at 40 mmcfd - Amoco.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Andrew gas flowing at 40 mmcfd - Amoco.

text.p: The volume of gas coming ashore at Teesside through the Amoco Corp-operated CATS pipeline has increased by 40 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) following the start up of the British Petroleum Co Plc- operated Andrew field in June, Amoco said on Wednesday.

Amoco said in a statement that CATS (the Central Area Transmission System) is now handling more than 340 mmcfd of gas through a 255-mile subsea pipeline. By 1998, it is scheduled to bring ashore 20 percent of the U.K.'s entire North Sea gas production.
Gas from Andrew, which is 150 miles east of Aberdeen, will come ashore at Teesside with existing flows of 300 mmcfd from Everest and Lomond.
The gas is being processed by Enron Europe Liquids Processing and gas from all three fields is being received by the Enron-operated combined heat and power plant.
Amoco said it was increasing processing capacity at the CATS terminal at Teesside to 1.2 billion cfd of gas and 2,000 tonnes a day of natural gas liquids by 1998.
